title: Nairobi October–December 2026 wet-season scenario
season: October–December 2026 (with rainfall in Nairobi expected to continue into January)
plain_summary: Weather agencies expect a wetter-than-average short-rains season in Nairobi, with possible spells of heavy rain. This gives us a reason to prepare, but does not tell us which streets will flood or how deep the water will be.

history_breakdown.title: Surface-water history
history_breakdown.detail: Satellite images show places where water has appeared repeatedly over the years.

history_breakdown.title: Rainfall history
history_breakdown.detail: Monthly rainfall records help compare places that have experienced unusually heavy rainfall. This information contributes to the concern score.

history_breakdown.title: The shape and use of the land
history_breakdown.detail: Maps show slopes, low ground and surfaces where more rain may flow over the ground instead of soaking in.

history_breakdown.title: Buildings and drains
history_breakdown.detail: Our saved OpenStreetMap data provides the mapped rivers, drains and building outlines used here.

outlook_facts.label: Nairobi rainfall
outlook_facts.detail: Kenya Met expects above-average rain in Nairobi. Its outlook also says spells of heavy rain are likely in affected counties.

outlook_facts.label: Expected start
outlook_facts.detail: Kenya Met expects rain to be fairly well spread through the season, continuing into January in Nairobi.

outlook_facts.label: Climate driver
outlook_facts.detail: In its 10 September 2026 advisory, NOAA put the chance of a very strong El Niño at more than 90% during late 2026 and early 2027. This is a forecast of El Niño strength, not Nairobi flood probability.

regional_context: The regional weather centre, ICPAC, reports a high chance of more than 400 mm of rain over the season in parts of central Kenya. That figure covers a wider region; it is not a rainfall total predicted for each Nairobi study area.

analogue_years.use: Primary Kenya analogue identified by KMSA for the combined ENSO and Indian Ocean conditions
Regional wet-season analogue identified by ICPAC
Regional wet-season analogue identified by ICPAC and already used in the historical satellite review

selected_model.name: Probabilistic rainfall-runoff and 2D flood scenario model
selected_model.why: It can turn several plausible 2026 storms into runoff, flow routes, water depth and affected-building ranges. A machine-learning forecast alone is not suitable because the project does not yet have enough checked flood-depth observations for training.
selected_model.current_status: The map uses the land, drainage and other local evidence to identify places needing closer review. It does not yet predict flood depth or the chance of flooding in 2026.
implementation: Build low, central and severe 2026 storm scenarios from official forecasts and historical rainfall.
Convert rainfall to runoff using land cover, soil and drainage condition.
Route runoff through a checked surface and drainage model.
Report a range of water depths and affected buildings, including uncertainty.
selected_model.preferred_tools: SWMM for drains linked to HEC-RAS 2D or LISFLOOD-FP for surface flow, after drainage levels and structures are checked.

rainfall_data_plan.status: Required; request from KMSA and Nairobi drainage teams

rainfall_data_plan.use: Build and check half-hourly storm shapes from 1998 to present
rainfall_data_plan.status: Available; 0.1° (~10 km), so it must be checked against gauges

rainfall_data_plan.use: Rank wet seasons and daily extremes from 1981 to near-present
rainfall_data_plan.status: Available; 0.05° and daily, not street-scale intensity

rainfall_data_plan.use: Represent the range of plausible OND 2026 rainfall, not one certain outcome
rainfall_data_plan.status: Available; regional forecast must be bias-corrected for Nairobi

bands.label: 0–31 m
bands.purpose: First inspection band because overflow and bank problems are most directly connected to the channel here.

bands.label: 31–62.5 m
bands.purpose: Shows how exposure changes beyond the channel edge and immediate bank area.

bands.label: 62.5–125 m
bands.purpose: Captures nearby low ground and possible overflow routes without treating the whole neighbourhood as river exposure.

buffer_method.explanation: We check land up to 125 metres on either side of a mapped river or drain. Splitting it into three distance bands helps compare building counts and plan visits as we move further from the waterway.
buffer_method.warning: These distance bands help us plan checks. They do not mark legal river reserves or show how far a flood will reach. Riverbanks still need to be checked on the ground.
